summary: A product entry in a fictional retro-industrial catalogue: a narrow 810px column of small Univers prose, each section paired with flat SVG 'marketing slides' in terminal colours (green, amber, red on black) and jQuery tab strips for code languages, document types and signature glyphs. It sells a coding monospace through use-case evidence (code, API docs, phone book, financial tables), a 1970s machine-type lineage, a post-purchase font compiler, developer testimonials and a licence table by company size.

instances.look: Static site header: 'U.S. Graphics Company' in condensed bold beside a strip of colour swatches (catalogue colour bar), and a row of six outlined button tabs (Office, ● Products, Catalog, Extras!, Sitemap, Login); a 'Products / Typefaces' breadcrumb sits below

Catalogue-entry layout: left half has 'Berkeley Mono™' heading, a yellow SKU tag 'TYPEFACE' and an outlined 'TX-02' tag, three short manifesto paragraphs and a green 'Datasheet (PDF) →' button; right half is a bordered card reading 'TX-02 / -------- / BERKELEY / MONO™ / TYPEFACE' in the font
instances.ux: Only CTA is the PDF datasheet; purchase is far below
instances.learn: Present the font like an industrial part (SKU, model number, datasheet) instead of a creative product: the framing itself tells programmers it is a tool

reconstruction.layout: 810px centred column (x=315); two equal columns (~395px) ~410px tall; text left; card right with 1px grey border and ~20px padding, 5 lines of ~60px type
reconstruction.typography: Heading ~16px Univers LT Pro Bold; SKU tags ~11px Berkeley Mono caps in small boxes; body 14px Univers, leading ~1.45; card lines ~60px Berkeley Mono Regular, dashed rule made of hyphens
reconstruction.content: 'Berkeley Mono™ is a love letter to the golden era of computing… It wears a UNIX T-shirt… It is Adrian Frutiger visits Bell Labs… Berkeley Mono is a typeface for professionals.'

instances.look: 'Engineered for Code': a strip of five outlined tabs (Generic, SQL, Haskell, Files, Finance) above a black panel of large green code ('@tick.tock! func Go( system::float $1, 3.2706 * x^2 - 4, 0xFC82 &| 0x1A9E ) return { i += 1, get["KEY"].run() };')
instances.ux: jQuery UI tabs swap the panel image per language or data type; on mobile the tab labels shorten to 1–5
instances.learn: Write fake code that packs the troublemakers (0/O, braces, operators, hex) into a few lines, and set it huge: a code font proves itself in code, not in pangrams

reconstruction.layout: Full column 810px; tab strip of 5 equal outlined buttons ~28px tall, active tab filled black; panel 810×~800px black with ~50px padding
reconstruction.typography: Code ~48px Berkeley Mono Regular, green #2bd47d-ish on black, 2-space indents; tab labels ~11px Univers
reconstruction.behaviour: Click tab → show its panel (jQuery UI tabs, aria-selected); panels are static SVGs
reconstruction.content: Invented code per tab: generic pseudo-language, SQL, Haskell, file listings, finance data

instances.learn: Argue legibility with a line-up of the characters programmers confuse (iI1lL, O0o, quotes, punctuation) rather than with adjectives
